caveats: The recipe box starts empty; a recipe gets in when a parent sends a link and says yes to saving it.
The fetch returns readable article text, not the page's embedded recipe data, so the model parses ingredients from prose and can drop a line; the source link is always included.
Some recipe sites sit behind bot walls or paywalls and return nothing; Happy says so instead of guessing.
The phone's reader view and recipe-keeper apps already clean up a recipe page; the added value is the hand-off to the shared grocery list and a plan fitted to the family calendar.
Happy does not know what is in the kitchen, so it offers the whole ingredient list and the parent strikes what they have.
Scaling quantities is arithmetic done by a language model: fine for a stew, worth a second look for baking.
The reading part works the day the research agent exists; the grocery hand-off waits on the Reminders bridge (F030) and the Sunday plan on the calendar connection (F009), and neither exists yet.
The schema fixes the shape of what research returns, not its content, and nothing in the platform forces that check to run.

The allergy fit is the model reading the family's allergy notes against each recipe's ingredient list. It can miss an allergen that sits inside an ingredient, so Happy is never the allergy authority and the cook still checks ingredients and labels.

demand_source.title: Renew an adult passport | USAGov
demand_source.supports: The federal guide tells people to renew early because some countries and airlines deny entry when a passport expires in less than six months, which is the case for a long-lead reminder.

edits.description: A monthly text lists what is coming due, each item appearing once its own lead time starts (a house choice of about nine months for an adult passport, shorter for inspection, registration, domains and Global Entry), with the official link. A child's passport lasts five years and cannot be renewed, so its row says 'apply again in person'. The same table holds each child's yearly check-up, home and car upkeep on a repeat interval (furnace filter, oil change), the end date of a policy or warranty a parent asked Happy to file, and any tax, benefit or gift dates a parent typed in. Nothing is renewed, booked or paid.
edits.how: Preferred build, in the pattern of the model-free watchers (F018): one monthly host command job per parent (`--command-argv`, no model call) runs a reviewed script that reads the dates table generated from family.json5, plus household-store rows (F031) once parents can add them, works out in code which rows are inside their lead time and prints one templated text, or `NO_REPLY` when nothing is due. The 9 Oct build note instead used a monthly isolated automation on the parent's agent with an empty tool list and the table in the job message; that leaves the date sums to the model, so keep it only as a fallback. Rows a parent adds by chat (a filed policy's end date, a typed benefit or gift date, 'did the furnace filter' restarting an upkeep interval) are written to the household store by the parent's own agent.
caveats: The build note has the dates table generated from Tony's registry, which a parent cannot change by chat. The carried-over extras that let a parent add a row ('file this as the car insurance policy', a typed benefit deadline) need either an edit by Tony or the household store (F031) as the table's home; decide which before building.
Reading a policy PDF to pull out its end date sends that document to the cloud model; whether that is acceptable is still an open decision.
If the fallback is used (a model run with no tools and the table in its prompt), the model works out the lead times itself and can get a date wrong; the script does the sums in code.
Command jobs are created by the operator and run on the Gateway host as the happy user, outside the sandbox, so the script is reviewed like the rest of the config repo.
edits.safety: With the script route no model is called to build the text; the delivered line may be mirrored into the receiving parent's session transcript, as with the watchers. Each parent's text comes from that parent's own job and goes only to them. Nothing is renewed, booked or paid: the text carries the official link and the parent acts. The one step that sends a document to the cloud model is reading a policy PDF to file its end date, which is still an open decision.
